releases.name: browsy-bot 0.2.0
releases.body:
## What's new

Tier 1 features on top of the multi-tool CDP core (v0.1.0). Same zero-middleware architecture — direct Chrome DevTools Protocol, no Puppeteer/Playwright/ChromeDriver.

### `browsy doctor`
Read-only diagnostics that tell you why nothing works. Probes CDP endpoint reachability, target/page count, browser-binary discovery, and memorius availability, then returns an actionable `DoctorReport` with next-step suggestions.

```bash
browsy doctor --json
# not ready: CDP endpoint ws://localhost:9222 is unreachable: ECONNREFUSED.
# Launch Chrome with: <chrome> --remote-debugging-port=9222 --headless --no-sandbox,
# or run "browsy ensure-browser" to start one for you.
```

### `browsy extract <selector> [field...]`
First-class structured data extraction — no more bespoke `Runtime.evaluate` boilerplate. One in-page script pulls typed records from every matching element, capped by `--limit`.

```bash
browsy extract "article.card" text "attr:src" value
# -> [ { "text": "...", "src": "...", "value": null }, ... ]
```

Field specs: `text`, `html`, `textContent`, `value`, or `attr:<name>`.

### `browsy ensure-browser` / `browsy stop-browser`
Self-service browser lifecycle. `ensure-browser` probes the endpoint; if it's down it spawns Chrome/Chromium on a **dedicated `user-data-dir`** under the browsy state dir (`$BROWSY_STATE_DIR` or `~/.browsy`) — never your logged-in profile — writes a pidfile, and polls `/json/version` until the CDP endpoint answers. `stop-browser` SIGTERMs the recorded pid and clears the pidfile.

```bash
browsy ensure-browser --port 9222 --no-headless
browsy stop-browser
```

### Trusted input (`--trusted`)
`click` and `fill` gain an opt-in `--trusted` flag that dispatches **renderer-trusted CDP input events** (`Input.dispatchMouseEvent` / `Input.insertText`) instead of JS-dispatched `el.click()` / `el.value =`. The page's event listeners see a user-originated input event. Default JS-dispatch path is unchanged for backward compatibility.

```bash
browsy click ".save" --trusted
browsy fill "#email" "a@b.c" --trusted
```

### API additions (library)
- `extract(session, selector, fields, { limit })` → `Record<string, unknown>[]`
- `doctor(browserUrl, options?)` → `DoctorReport`; probes `probeVersion`, `findBrowserBinary`, `checkMemorius` are exported too
- `ensureBrowser` / `launchBrowser` / `stopBrowser` / `buildBrowserArgs` / `resolveBrowserBinary` / `waitForReady`
- `click` / `fill` now accept `{ trusted?: boolean }`

## Notes
- **78/78 tests** (up from 49 in v0.1.0) — new suites for diagnostics, extraction, and browser lifecycle; trusted-input cases in the actions suite.
- **Security:** the CDP endpoint is still full browser control. `ensure-browser` is profile-scoped to keep the blast radius small; the `--trusted` path carries a TOCTOU caveat (see the Security section of the README).
- **CLI exit codes unchanged:** `0` success, `1` runtime/CDP failure, `2` usage error, `3` CDP connection failure.

releases.name: browsy-bot 0.1.0
releases.body: Tool-agnostic CDP core + MCP server + hardened CLI. Zero-middleware CDP browser automation: one core, three adapters (OpenCode plugin, universal MCP server, CLI with --json). Memorius learning, portable skill. The tag-triggered release workflow is in place; npm publish needs a valid NPM_TOKEN in repo secrets.
